statusDefinitions.not_started: No usable editor workflow exists yet.
statusDefinitions.prototype: A visible or headless slice exists, but major workflow pieces, coverage, or consumer proof are missing.
statusDefinitions.functional: The workflow has real ViewModel behavior, source-backed or consumer-backed state where applicable, and required automated tests for current behavior.
statusDefinitions.figma_grade: The workflow meets the M32 quality bar for dense, discoverable, keyboardable, visually asserted, low-latency editor UX.
statusDefinitions.validated_in_metacraft: The workflow is figma_grade and has passed the live metacraft-web consumer matrix for the same behavior.

criteria: Sidebar shows at least 10 meaningful rows on a 900px-tall viewport without marketing copy.
Inspector shows at least 14 editable or diagnostic rows on a 768px-tall viewport before scrolling.
Primary canvas remains the dominant surface after opening one side panel.
Every icon-only control has an accessible name and hover/focus tooltip.
Disabled controls expose an inline diagnostic or command-state reason.
Current mode, selected element, write status, and source scope are visible without opening a modal.
Core workflows are reachable by Tab, arrow-key roving focus where appropriate, Enter/Space activation, and Escape dismissal.
Keyboard selection and command execution produce the same ViewModel state as pointer execution.
Focus returns to the invoking control after closing popovers, dialogs, and transient editors.
Sidebar and inspector support pointer resize, keyboard resize, collapse, and restore.
Panel widths persist within a session and clamp to documented min/max values.
Canvas and iframe content reflow without overlapping chrome during resize.
Hover feedback is visible within 50ms on representative metacraft-web pages.
Selection-to-inspector update completes within 100ms for representative nested component DOM.
Vector canvas selection feedback completes within one animation frame for common symbol documents.
Mode changes, selection changes, validation messages, and save state changes do not shift persistent toolbar or panel anchors.
Loading and empty states reserve stable dimensions.
No unexpected body scrollbars appear at supported desktop and tablet breakpoints.

features.title: Edit and View Commands
features.targetWorkflow: Users can activate Edit, Inspect, Comment, Save, Revert, and related commands by pointer and keyboard, with clear enablement diagnostics tied to the current selection and workspace capability.
features.implementation: Typed command availability, dispatch, diagnostics, URL state, keyboard and pointer activation.
features.knownLimitations: Command palette coverage, tooltip consistency, and full focus-return behavior remain M42 work.

screenshotVisualAssertions.notes: Needs stable visual baselines for hover, focus, disabled, running, and failed command states.

evidence: tests/browser/specs/metacraft-web-editor.spec.ts:mounts the live consumer workspace through public editor APIs

features.title: CSS Property Editors
features.targetWorkflow: Users can inspect, validate, stage, undo, redo, and save representative CSS properties through typed editor state and source plans.
features.implementation: Typed CSS value parsing, primitive-control normalization, math-expression/unit handling, source-plan selection, validation, shared-scope handling, undo/redo, dirty state, save staging, raw CSS section editing, cascade origin indicators, copy/paste/reset property actions, numeric select-all/arrow/scrub/unit controls, color swatches/formats/variable/token/contrast affordances, gradient stop/angle/type controls, shadow layer/crosshair/inset/elevation controls, typography style/responsive/truncate/wrap controls, border-radius linked-corner controls, and Bezier/reduced-motion motion controls with live iframe preview and source commits.
features.knownLimitations: M36 is a meaningful functional vertical slice. Advanced browser polish is still incomplete for full Figma/Webflow parity: no visual-baseline screenshots, no full color-plane/gradient drag serialization suite, no complete canvas radius handles, no browser eyedropper integration, no draggable Bezier editor, and mobile inspector controls collapse rather than proving visible mobile editing. Browser save coverage is representative for schema-backed controls; fallback primitive additions are staged and reverted until the consumer source schema owns those properties. Status stays functional until M32 screenshot/visual evidence gates are satisfied.

playwrightTests.name: edits real metacraft component DOM through the inspector

screenshotVisualAssertions.notes: M36 adds functional primitive controls and DOM layout-overlap checks, but figma_grade still requires screenshot visual baselines for color, gradient, shadow, typography, border, motion, raw CSS, cascade states, and mobile visible-control behavior.

evidence: tests/browser/specs/metacraft-web-editor.spec.ts:edits real metacraft component DOM through the inspector

features.title: Layout, Auto Layout, Constraints, and Responsive Editing
features.targetWorkflow: Users can plan and apply representative flex, grid, constraint, canvas-guide, and viewport-scoped layout edits through source-aware editor contracts and live component preview controls.
features.implementation: M37 adds framework layout-control capabilities for flex/auto layout, grid, constraints, responsive modes, and canvas guides; source-aware planning routes edits to token, class, style/schema, story fixture, responsive mode, Tailwind, or fallback inline paths according to the M35 ownership graph. Browser coverage exposes functional layout controls, live iframe style updates, spacing measurement, gap overlays, snap lines, resize handles, and viewport-mode override staging.
features.knownLimitations: Functional M37 evidence is not full Figma-grade layout editing. Browser controls are representative and source-plan backed where the selected source map/schema owns the property; fallback DOM selections may stage local plans until the consumer schema owns every layout property. Canvas guides are DOM overlays, not screenshot-baselined visual assertions. Drag coverage proves resize-handle behavior, but not complete multi-axis constraint solving, advanced named-area editing, or full responsive visual baselines. Status remains functional until M32/M43 visual gates are satisfied.

screenshotVisualAssertions.notes: Needs visual baselines for layout controls, canvas guides, resize handles, snap lines, responsive mode switching, and no-overlap behavior before claiming Figma-grade.

features.title: Real Component DOM Editing
features.targetWorkflow: Users can select real rendered component DOM in a preview iframe, map the selection to source metadata, edit representative properties, and save through the consumer workspace adapter.
features.implementation: Component edit mode renders the project-owned preview iframe, installs a generic DOM selection and hover-inspection bridge with selection handles, supports source-backed stable element identities, deep element selection, repeat-click parent cycling, Shift-click component wrapper selection, keyboard parent/child/next/previous/clear traversal, a searchable/expandable Layers tree, hover-to-highlight, breadcrumb/source-path context, layer and breadcrumb ancestor selection by the same identity, selection restoration across mode/browser viewport/save/revert cycles, maps clicked real DOM to InspectorVM source-backed properties, applies inspector edits live in the iframe, and routes representative edits through the workspace source adapter with dirty/save/revert state.
features.knownLimitations: Marquee/multi-select is only model-ready, hidden/locked rows are readiness flags rather than enforcement, and visual latency/screenshot baselines remain future gate work.

playwrightTests.name: edits real metacraft component DOM through the inspector

screenshotVisualAssertions.notes: M33 has behavior coverage for selection, layers, breadcrumbs, and restore paths. Figma-grade still needs screenshot assertions for hover rings, selected handles, breadcrumbs, iframe reflow, and no layout jumping.

evidence: tests/browser/specs/metacraft-web-editor.spec.ts:edits real metacraft component DOM through the inspector

features.title: Foundation Token Editors
features.targetWorkflow: Users can edit design-system tokens, inspect impact, validate contrast and alias cycles, and stage source-backed changes.
features.implementation: Token edits, impact analysis, contrast validation, semantic alias cycle validation, and source-plan generation.
features.knownLimitations: Token manager UI, searchable swatches, variable binding, usage previews, and visual baselines remain M36/M43 work.
features.playwrightReason: Current coverage is a headless source/schema contract; Figma-grade token manager UX requires new browser workflows in M36.

screenshotVisualAssertions.notes: Needs token manager, contrast, alias, impact, and dependency visual baselines.

features.title: Component Variant Editors
features.targetWorkflow: Users can edit component variant metadata, fixtures, states, responsive samples, and generated source plans.
features.implementation: M38 extends the component variant editor with schema-backed component properties for enum, boolean, text, icon, slot/content, data fixture, density, platform, and accessibility labels; state controls for size, emphasis, tone, selected, disabled, hover, focus, pressed, loading, empty, error, success, and project-specific states; structured source plans for schema/fixture/source constructors; variant matrix previews; actionable coverage diagnostics; create-story-for-state commands; per-property documentation and usage guidance; and shared AI/manual pending edit journal context.
features.knownLimitations: Functional M38 coverage is not Figma-grade. Browser coverage uses the live metacraft-web component preview path with runtime schema inference when the consumer has not supplied a full component-property schema, so it proves source-plan routing, matrix/state controls, save/revert, and diagnostics without claiming complete Figma-grade component API extraction, screenshot baselines, or exhaustive visual comparison across every component/state.

screenshotVisualAssertions.notes: M38 has functional browser interaction coverage, but Figma-grade still needs screenshot baselines for the property panel, matrix cells, state controls, missing-story commands, diagnostics, save/revert states, and mobile layout.

features.title: Style, Class, Cascade, and Token Manager
features.targetWorkflow: Users can inspect class stacks, reusable styles, cascade/source layers, token aliases/modes/usages/impact, and choose safe edit scopes that stage source-backed plans.
features.implementation: M39 adds framework ViewModel contracts for current class stacks, reusable style search data, create/rename/duplicate/detach/promote/tokenize source plans, cascade layers with final/inherited/overridden/editable/source/token-chain details, token manager items with aliases, modes, usage, impact, contrast diagnostics, dependent stories, safe scope choices, and diagnostics for one-off token candidates, duplicate classes, hardcoded token matches, and unsafe detachments. The browser inspector exposes the style manager in the Source / Cascade panel and verifies local/shared scope choices update the live metacraft-web preview with save/revert.
features.knownLimitations: Functional M39 coverage is not Figma-grade or Webflow/Figma parity. The UI is a compact inspector panel rather than a full class selector popover with rich keyboard roving, drag/drop class stack management, screenshot baselines, or exhaustive visual regression coverage. Browser coverage proves one real metacraft-web scope-change path plus save/revert; full token-manager impact previews, searchable swatch visuals, and screenshot/visual assertions remain below the M32 Figma-grade gate.

screenshotVisualAssertions.notes: Needs screenshot baselines for class selector/search/create/rename/duplicate/detach/promote flows, cascade/source layers, token manager aliases/modes/impact/contrast, diagnostics, save/revert states, and mobile inspector layout before claiming Figma-grade.

features.title: Inline Canvas Manipulation and Direct Editing
features.targetWorkflow: Users can manipulate selected preview elements directly on the canvas for representative resize, spacing, reorder, inline text, and context-menu actions while edits are staged as source-backed plans.
features.implementation: M40 adds typed direct-canvas operation contracts for resize, spacing, reorder, inline text, and selection context commands. Resize and spacing route through the M37 layout ownership planner when project schema ownership is present, inline text and context commands route through M35 source ownership where available, and metacraft-web consumer previews fall back to the existing generic source-map adapter without mutating DOM-only state. Browser coverage uses the live metacraft-web editable iframe with pointer resize, spacing-handle drag, drag reorder, inline text editing, context-menu actions, and the shared inspector undo/save/revert journal.
features.knownLimitations: This is functional M40 coverage, not full Figma-grade direct manipulation. The browser handles and menu are representative rather than fully polished, reorder is a source-backed order edit rather than a complete drag/drop list authoring system, metacraft-web currently exposes a generic source-map adapter rather than exhaustive per-property design schema ownership, and screenshot/visual assertions for handles, overlays, context-menu polish, collision avoidance, and mobile behavior remain below the M32/M43 visual gate.

screenshotVisualAssertions.notes: Needs screenshot baselines for direct resize handles, spacing overlays, reorder feedback, inline text editing state, context menu commands, save/revert states, and mobile canvas behavior before claiming Figma-grade.

features.title: SVG and Vector Editors
features.targetWorkflow: Users can select, transform, edit, import, optimize, and save vector symbols through a library-backed canvas and source-backed ViewModel bridge.
features.implementation: Fabric-backed canvas interaction, Paper.js-backed boolean/path-segment operations, SVGO-backed export, source-backed properties, undo/redo, diagnostics for unsupported freeform Bezier editing, and M27 save bridging.
features.knownLimitations: Full Penpot-grade layer panel, snapping, keyboard editing polish, and complete Bezier path workflows remain future quality work.

screenshotVisualAssertions.notes: Needs baselines for canvas selection, layers, handles, transforms, boolean ops, import state, and no blank canvas.

evidence: tests/browser/specs/metacraft-web-editor.spec.ts:mounts the live consumer workspace through public editor APIs

features.title: Workspace Source Synchronization
features.targetWorkflow: Users can stage source edits, save them transactionally through a consumer adapter, recover from conflicts, and refresh targeted preview state.
features.implementation: Adapter-mediated transactions, same-file composition, conflicts, rollback, targeted reload, full reload fallback, generated-view roundtrip, M42 dev-server bridge endpoints for dry-run/apply/save/revert with external-change detection and rollback-on-failure coverage, and reload-generation selection restoration after real source writes.
features.knownLimitations: M42 is functional development-workspace fidelity, not production/Figma-grade collaboration. Static/browser-only builds remain staging-only unless a project write bridge is configured; visual screenshots for saving/conflict states and multi-user collaborative rebasing remain future work.

features.title: Agent-Assisted Edits
features.targetWorkflow: Users can collect design-review comments on selected canvas elements, choose which comments to send to AI, review scoped agent proposals, accept or reject changes, and save accepted patches through the same source adapter path.
features.implementation: Structured prompt context, ACP/Agent Harbor event mapping through nim-agents, permission state, proposal review, partial accept, reject, revert, cancel, error, completion, M27 save path, M41 structured review annotations with selected element identity, viewport/screenshot/DOM snapshot metadata, source ownership, include/exclude prompt selection, open/resolved/dismissed state, design-system constraints, selected schema/token/component/variant context, proposal scope/impact/tests metadata, and proposal rebase diagnostics after overlapping manual edits.
features.knownLimitations: Functional M41 coverage is not full Figma-grade design review. Comment markers are DOM overlays without screenshot baseline assertions, screenshot context is a reference captured by the iframe bridge rather than an attached bitmap, metacraft-web currently proves structured comment selection on its live preview but not a production agent acceptance path, and the proposal diff/impact/tests UI is compact rather than a rich side-by-side diff reviewer. Visual baselines, production agent setup, richer diff review UI, collaborative comment presence, and mobile visual assertions remain below the M32/M43 gates.

playwrightTests.name: comment mode stores structured review annotations for AI prompt selection

screenshotVisualAssertions.notes: Needs baselines for empty, streaming, permission, comment pins, include/exclude states, resolved/dismissed states, diff review, accepted, rejected, stale/rebase, and error states.

features.title: Design-System Schema and Source Ownership
features.targetWorkflow: Users and agents can resolve selected DOM properties to project-owned design schema nodes, source spans, generated views, classes, Tailwind utilities, and fallback edit paths before staging shared changes.
features.implementation: Versioned schema contracts, token modes, source ownership graph resolution, usage/affected-surface impact calculation, review-level escalation, contrast diagnostics, and unstructured-source migration diagnostics.
features.knownLimitations: M35 is a headless framework contract and fixture-backed boundary proof. Concrete metacraft-web schema files, preview/story wiring, visual controls, and browser editing UX remain M36-M41 work.
features.playwrightReason: M35 is a headless schema/source ownership contract; browser controls and consumer story wiring are planned for M36-M41.

screenshotVisualAssertions.notes: Needs visual baselines for token pickers, source ownership badges, usage previews, impact warnings, and migration diagnostics before Figma-grade status.

features.title: Visual Regression, Screenshot, and UX Review Gates
features.targetWorkflow: Maintainers can run an automated visual gate that captures representative editor modes, checks nonblank canvas/iframe surfaces, rejects obvious clipping, overlap, unreachable controls, and body scroll regressions, then emits a reviewer brief for changed screenshots and failed UX-density checks.
features.implementation: M43 adds Playwright screenshot baselines for shell, AI proposal mode, Comment popover mode, Edit inspector, token/style/layers panels, component variant matrix, narrow right panel, and vector editor across desktop, laptop, tablet, and mobile-width viewports. It also adds canvas-pixel checks, selected-element/handle/popover assertions, no-body-scroll/no-clipping/no-overlap checks, mode-switch panel stability checks, and a Node visual-review brief generator.
features.knownLimitations: The gate is a meaningful automated visual regression baseline for the current editor surfaces, but rows remain functional rather than Figma-grade until M44 keyboard/accessibility/performance coverage and M45 mature release evidence are complete. Metacraft-web keeps its own project-specific browser coverage through the consumer suite.

assertions: Screenshot baselines cover shell desktop/laptop/tablet/mobile-width, AI proposal mode, comment popover mode, edit inspector token/style/layers panels, component variant matrix, narrow right panel, and vector editor.
Canvas and iframe checks prove vector previews are nonblank and selected component previews expose visible selection, handles, layout guides, and comment popovers.
UX quality checks reject body scroll regressions, essential overlap, clipped controls, and right-panel layout shifts after mode switches.
screenshotVisualAssertions.notes: M43 establishes automated screenshot and UX-review gates for the current primary editor surfaces; later milestones decide whether individual workflows can be promoted to Figma-grade.
